newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Japan, Korea to invest $3.8 bln in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Japan, Korea to invest $3.8 bln in Latin America.

text.p: Japanese and South Korean investors have plans to invest about $3.8 billion in heavy industry projects in Latin America, much of which is bound for Venezuela, a top Venezuelan government official said on Tuesday.

"The Korean and Japanese projects already defined for Latin America total $3.8 billion of which a large share refers to steel, iron and aluminum in Venezuela," Elias Nadim Ynaty, president of state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) told reporters in Congress.

Ynaty, who recently returned from a trip to Japan and South Korea, highlighted a decision by South Korea's Posco Chemical Co Ltd to go ahead with a 1.5 million tonnes per year hot briquetted iron (HBI) plant in Venezuela in which it will have a controlling stake.
